newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada heavy oil field sparks hot company interest. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Canada heavy oil field sparks hot company interest. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]

text.p: A heavy oil field in Alberta, estimated to be the largest oil find in the province in decades, is sparking huge interest among several producers willing to shell out big money to get a piece of the action.

The Pelican Lake field in northeastern Alberta, which analysts estimate could harbor 3 billion barrels of oil in place and 400 million barrels of recoverable oil, took center stage at the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers investment symposium on Monday.
(Corrects estimated reserve potential from "10 billion barrels of oil in place and 2 billion barrels of recoverable oil")
The hot interest comes despite a deepening discount for heavy oil compared to light crude.

"This particular asset is going to be a prize in Alberta, probably the 8th largest oil field ever found (in the province) and certainly the largest since about 1964," Scott Inglis, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital Corp, said in an interview. "It's a high-quality, low-cost asset with a lot of recoverable reserve potential."

Companies such as Canadian Natural Resources Ltd and Alberta Energy Co Ltd disclosed the sky-high prices they paid for land in the region, which became hot after junior oil company Amber Energy Inc recently announced major reserve increases.
AEC chief executive Gwyn Morgan said his firm spent about C$16 million at the same record land sale on a parcel to the north which is about a third the size of Canadian Natural's.

Inglis said prices paid for the Pelican Lake acreage, at about C$1,000 an acre, are 10 times the average paid for rights to drill on land in Alberta, which in itself is already up 50 percent over last year.
"Our plan would be to go in and develop that over that over the next two drilling seasons. We'll probably have about 150 to 170 locations to drill on that acreage," MacPhail said.
He said the company did not plan to start high-tech drilling and steam injection production techniques on the lands immediately, which are estimated to have 1.2 billion barrels of oil in place.
Morgan said it was early to say what the reserve potential was in AEC's Pelican acreage, although he said he assumed it would be proportional to Canadian Natural's lands.
MacPhail said Canadian Natural was not interested in launching a rival bid for CS, despite the company's growing position at Pelican Lake.
While Morgan said he would not comment on specific deals, he said there was "not a very high probability" that a corporate acquisition was in the cards for AEC this year.
CS has said it would soon be in a position to announce a strategic alliance in attempts to thwart Gulf's bid.

The question mark clouding investment at Pelican Lake and in Canada's booming heavy oil activity in general remained the widening price differential between light and heavy crude, now at about US$6.50 per barrel between West Texas Intermediate and Lloydminster heavy blend, Inglis said.

But, with growing heavy output from Canada, Venezuela and Mexico, refiners would likely be required to add the necessary processing capability over the next few years, which could bring heavy prices closer to light oil again, he said.
